messages.subject: Analysing multiple years of data
parts:
Hi

I am undertaking a project where we are comparing population estimates of =
over abundant kangaroos derived from 3 different methods. Ground surveys a=
nalysed using Distance. Ground surveys analysed using WildlifeDensity (alt=
ernative analysis engine). Aerial surveys analysed using Distance!

I currently want to analyse the ground survey data using Distance. I have =
3 years of survey data. Two areas (Mournpall & Outside Mournpall) are surv=
eyed and both Red & Western Grey Kangaroos are recorded; each year. Number=
s of Red Kangaroos in the smaller of the 2 areas (41km=B2) are low each yea=
r and therefore I wish to pool then post stratify the data.

I am seeking advice on the best way to undertake the analysis. Should I po=
ol the 3 years of Red kangaroo data in the Mournpall area then post stratif=
y by year? And if I separate the Red & Grey data for an individual survey,=
do I need to show all the survey effort where there were no Reds? Or is t=
here an alternative way I could undertake this analysis?

I have previously undertaken the analysis for each individual year, but I'm=
hoping to increase the precision of the estimates by combining the data.

Thank you for your advice

Regards
Lorraine

messages.author: 27dad1e4c5016b3e
messages.subject: Re: Analysing multiple years of data
parts:
Hi All

I have provided some further information below to my original email, which =
I hope will add to the background information I have already provided.

I require as an end result a population estimate for each species in both a=
reas for each year. This data will be used to compare pop. est. derived us=
ing the same data from an alternative analysis engine.

Prevoiusly 2 years of data has been pooled but the CV for red kangaroos was=
as high as 43.6% in one area. Hence Im seeking tips to how to get the bes=
t possible population estimates using the data I have, whether that be by =
seperating the red & grey data or areas. Total observations of reds in Mou=
rnpall area over the 3 years =3D 62 and in the Outside Mournpall area =3D43=
. Grey observations are higher.

I will analyse the data for both reds and greys seperately in the two areas=
; 6 strata (3 years x 2 areas) ; fit global detection function, then stratu=
m specific encounter rates based on advice I have received

Thank you
